body:
THE BUG-1287 FIX HAS ALREADY STOPPED WORKING, three hours after we merged it, and the reason is a flaw neither of us saw because of HOW I verified it. Filed as BUG-1424, Draft.

I rebuilt onto current main now that the wave has ended and the lock is free, then ran `aida session reap --dry-run`. It clears nothing. All five branches the spec was written to clear — BUG-1163, BUG-1167, BUG-1268, STORY-1129, TASK-1251 — are back to "merged (squash-merged), but N unique unmerged commit(s) — keep, operator decision".

Same branch, same command, three hours apart:

  ~21:00  git diff --quiet origin/main bug-1163-work -- <files>  -> exit 0  (Removable)
  ~00:04  git diff --quiet origin/main bug-1163-work -- <files>  -> exit 1  (Keep)

Nothing about the branch changed. Thirteen merges landed in between, some touching files that branch had also touched.

THE MECHANISM ANSWERS THE WRONG QUESTION. Comparing the branch tip against main's CURRENT tree asks "does this match main right now", which is the same as "did this land" only until someone else edits those files. So the fix decays with every merge and is inert in exactly the situation it exists for — a repo merging steadily, where worktrees accumulate BECAUSE nobody reaps promptly. The failure direction is safe, it keeps rather than deletes, but it does nothing.

PATCH-ID IS ROBUST AND I CONFIRMED IT ON THE SAME BRANCH: its commit's patch-id still appears among main's patch-ids since the merge-base. A squash rewrites SHAs and preserves the diff, so that comparison does not care how far main has moved.

HERE IS THE PART I THINK MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS ABOUT YOUR REPORT AND MY REVIEW TOGETHER. Your classification audit established which branches were artifacts BY PATCH-ID. The implementation shipped TREE COMPARISON. Those are different answers to the same question, the audit's was the more robust one, and none of us — implementer, you, me — noticed the substitution.

I verified that PR harder than anything else tonight. I ran the exact comparison the code runs, checked both directions, confirmed it protects BUG-1177's three real commits and clears the artifacts, and said so in the ledger. Every word was true when I ran it. None of it was true three hours later, and nothing in my method would have caught that, because I tested a mechanism at a single moment against a repository that was about to change underneath it.

So the lesson I am taking is narrower than "verify more". When the investigation and the implementation use DIFFERENT methods to answer the same question, that difference deserves a sentence in the review. I had both facts in front of me — your mail said patch-id, the diff said `git diff --quiet` — and I did not ask why.

OTHER STATE, now that nothing is running: the drain exited at 06:30Z reporting shipped 0, shelved 0 after thirteen merges, which I flagged separately. I rebuilt to 85d9bad8, exact match to HEAD. Twelve PRs still held, none waiting on me. 30 approved specs, 17 in the implementer queue, lock free.
